第 38 章 Ground Rules in Meetings会议中的基本规则

Lara Hogan / 劳拉·霍根

— 第 115 页 —

Research shows that all human groups use rules of engagement to make something that can be very unpredictable (humans and human conversations) be a little more predictable. —Paloma Medina, Ground Rules 101

研究表明，所有人类群体都使用参与规则来让本来非常不可预测的事情（人类和人类对话）变得稍微可预测一点。——Paloma Medina，《Ground Rules 101》

When you're in a meeting with six or more people, you might find that the group dynamics become a little unstable. One person looks checked out: they're on their laptop, you can hear Slack dinging. The person dialed in over video has stopped asking, "Could you move closer to the microphone, please?" and has resigned themselves to not being able to participate in this meeting. Another person has now dominated the conversation, continuing to make the same point in new and different ways.

当你在一个六个人或更多人的会议上时，你可能发现群体动态变得有点不稳定。一个人看起来心不在焉：在看笔记本电脑，你能听到 Slack 响。视频接入的人已经不再问「能请你靠近麦克风一点吗？」，已经认命无法参与这个会议。另一个人现在主导了对话，用各种新方式反复说同一个观点。

Ground rules are here to help. When I'm facilitating a meeting, I usually pick three to five ground rules to rally everyone around at the beginning, customizing them to the needs of the meeting (what's needed for us to make progress, or keep things on track, or collaborate effectively, etc.). As I learned from Medina, ground rules should be short and easy to remember, but avoid being overly cutesy or gimmicky. Use ground rules to keep the meeting on track toward its goal. Here are the common ways I use ground rules and some examples you can use right away!

基本规则就是来帮忙的。当我主持会议时，我通常在开始时选三到五条基本规则来凝聚大家，根据会议需求定制（我们需要什么来取得进展、保持正轨、有效协作等）。正如我从 Medina 那里学到的，基本规则应该简短好记，但避免过于可爱或花哨。用基本规则让会议朝目标前进。以下是我使用基本规则的常见方式和一些你可以立刻用的例子！

  • Attend on time, every time每次都准时参加
  • Optimize for deciding and acting以决策和行动为优化目标

You can also use ground rules to help attendees self-manage their participation and attention, especially when you have remote participants:

你还可以用基本规则帮参会者自我管理参与和注意力，尤其是有远程参与者时：

No laptops/phones/smartwatch alerts. Unless you're remote, in which case, please keep only this video window open.

不用笔记本电脑/手机/智能手表提醒。除非你是远程，那样的话请只开这个视频窗口。

— 第 116 页 —

Use hand signals to participate. Point to the ceiling to add something new, point at the person who's currently speaking to add on to their point, and use "jazz hands" when you can't hear or something else has gone wrong.

用手势参与。指向天花板表示要补充新内容，指向正在说话的人表示要补充他们的观点，用「爵士手」表示听不到或出了别的问题。

And you may also have ground rules to help attendees feel safer as they share information:

你还可以有基本规则帮参会者在分享信息时更有安全感：

Vegas rules. What happens in this meeting, stays in this meeting.

维加斯规则。会议里发生的事留在会议里。

Stay curious. Use open questions. Listen to learn.

保持好奇。用开放式问题。倾听是为了学习。

Ground rules are the foundation for all that comes afterward: they might inform who you invite to a meeting, shape resulting deliverables, and affect the ways in which you achieve the meeting's goal. For example, when I ran a working group for Meetup to help define the company's architecture principles, I wanted to emphasize that we were using a representative leadership model. I included these ground rules:

基本规则是之后一切的基础：它们可能影响你邀请谁参会、塑造产出物、以及影响你实现会议目标的方式。例如，当我为 Meetup 运营一个工作组来帮定义公司架构原则时，我想强调我们在用代表制领导模式。我加入了这些基本规则：

Optimize for deciding and acting. This is one of Meetup's company values. Reinforcing it as a ground rule helped the group avoid a potential failure mode in which participants optimized for full consensus, which would have dragged out our process indefinitely.

以决策和行动为优化目标。这是 Meetup 的公司价值观之一。把它作为基本规则强化帮团队避免了一个潜在失败模式——参与者追求完全共识，那会把我们的流程无限拉长。

You're representing a part of Meetup Engineering; speak for them, not just for you. We weren't there to voice personal opinions; we were there to represent a subset of the organization.

你代表 Meetup 工程部的一部分；为他们说话，不只是为你自己。我们不是来表达个人意见的；我们是来代表组织的一个子集的。

Let's act transparently. This was a cue for each representative to keep their subset of the organization informed of our working group's progress. Everything that happened in the room was fully shareable outside of it, too.

让我们透明行动。这是给每个代表的提示，让他们让自己代表的那部分组织了解工作组的进展。房间里发生的一切也完全可以分享到外面。

Remind participants of the ground rules at the top of every meeting so that they become baked in and won't slip over time. As the facilitator or meeting leader, curb behavior during the meeting that breaks a ground rule. It's okay if this is awkward—I promise, it becomes easier as the rules are enforced because the group begins to remember them more and help curb one another, too.

每次会议开始时提醒参会者基本规则，让它们深入人心、不会随时间淡忘。作为主持人或会议领导，在会议中制止违反基本规则的行为。如果这有点尴尬也没关系——我保证，随着规则被执行，它会变得更容易，因为团队开始更记住它们，也会互相提醒。

— 第 117 页 —

Apply ground rules today to help achieve your meeting goals fairly and effectively. Ground rules can of course change over time: new folks are introduced and meeting goals might shift to warrant new rules. As Medina says, spending a bit of time at the outset setting these rules of engagement "consistently sets a foundation for human-friendly communication and minimizes the need for mind reading."

今天就应用基本规则来公平有效地实现会议目标。基本规则当然可以随时间改变：新人加入、会议目标可能转变需要新规则。正如 Medina 所说，一开始花点时间设定这些参与规则「一致地为人友好的沟通奠定基础，最小化读心术的需要」。
